_meta.notes: Cho and Gall are one in game hero (Cho'gall) with two bodies; Icy Veins and Heroes Profile list them together, so their patch stats are shared.

Abathur.strengths_note: Toxic Nest, Symbiote and Deep Tunnel wage a non stop war across the map.
Abathur.weaknesses_note: Very low personal impact and hard to learn.
wants: melee assassins or bruisers as Symbiote hosts (Illidan, Greymane, Genji)
a team that is comfortable playing a man down in fights
a team that can push as four while he soaks
a map with several lanes and frequent objectives
gives: huge experience soak from several lanes
free shield and heal on the host
map wide vision and lane pressure
Ultimate Evolution clone
weak: weak early game
cannot solo a lane
body is very fragile if found
very map dependent
team must adapt to a man down style

good_into.why: Toxic Nest is a hidden mine that reveals and dismounts, and Spike Burst reveals cloaked units. The guide says nests are excellent against ganking heroes that use stealth.
Vile Nest slows by 40 percent and Envenomed Spikes slows all enemies hit, so melee hosts stick and enemy rotations are delayed. Heroes without a dash cannot answer a Symbiote assassin.
Deep Tunnel, Toxic Nest vision and Calldown: MULE (repairs structures, strong on Sky Temple) let him contest objectives while soaking. Locusts force a response on the other lane.

bad_into.why: Zeratul, Medivh, Genji and Nova can hunt his body in a lane. His body is extremely fragile if found, and Deep Tunnel needs a 3 second channel that can be interrupted.
The guide names Sylvanas, Zarya and Sgt. Hammer: heroes that push down a lane as four and have strong wave clear punish him. His whole plan is to be in more places than the enemy.
Symbiote is cancelled if the host dies or he is stunned, so a dive on the host removes everything he provides. Spike Burst and Stab are short ranged.
Stab and Spike Burst are short range and need a melee host. A kiter keeps the host out of range and Carapace is wasted.

Alarak.strengths_note: Discord Strike, Lightning Surge and Deadly Charge give strong single target burst.
Alarak.weaknesses_note: Demands precise ability use and has weak waveclear.
wants: A tank or hard CC hero to follow up on displaced targets
Allies who clear waves for him (Jaina, Raynor style)
A healer to keep him near full health for Ruthless Momentum
Burst follow up so a Telekinesis target dies
gives: Displacement that drags a target out of position into the team
A 1.5 second silence that strips an escape or a channel
Burst damage on a single priority target
Map hazard setups with Telekinesis
weak: Poor waveclear and cannot solo mercenary camps
Discord Strike has a delay and a narrow shape so it is hard to land
Loses all Sadism from takedown and quest sources on death
Stuns and silences deny his entire kit
Needs allies who can follow his displacement

good_into.why: The Overwhelming Power build with Hindered Motion and Mocking Strikes punishes heroes who must stay in his reach, and Telekinesis shoves them out of position for a Discord Strike silence.
Telekinesis into Discord Strike silences a squishy target for 1.5 seconds with Sadism doubling the damage, and the silence also blocks escapes.
Discord Strike silences, which shuts off blinks and dashes, and Dissonance adds 0.75 seconds; Telekinesis can pull an escaping hero back into the combo.
The Combo build uses Telekinesis on tanks to drag them out of their team, and Discord Strike silences their engage abilities with a follow up from allies.

bad_into.why: Stuns and silences from Johanna or E.T.C. stop Discord Strike, Telekinesis and Counter-Strike from being cast, and a deleted combo leaves a low health assassin with no peel.
He has no defensive kit between engages and Sadism is lost on death, so being chipped down before a fight is very costly.
Without Applied Force he struggles to reach ranged heroes and the Discord Strike delay is easy for them to side step.
Discord Strike has a 0.5 second delay and a cone shape, so heroes who retreat and dodge turn his only single target silence into a miss.

Alexstrasza.strengths_note: Gift of Life, Abundance and Dragonqueen give strong team sustain and burst.
Alexstrasza.weaknesses_note: Needs time to build heals and depends on positioning.
wants: A frontline with high maximum Health, since Abundance and Life Unbound heal by percent
Reliable crowd control, because she has no hard CC and no unstoppable
A team that holds its fight until Dragonqueen is ready
Peel that keeps divers off her during the transform
gives: Large percent based healing that scales with tanks and bruisers
Wave clear and lane pressure from Flame Buffet
Dragonqueen as a once a minute fight winner at objectives
Armor from Tough Love, shields from Overprotective, a cheat death with Blessing of the Red
weak: No cleanse and no unstoppable
Healing drops when she is damaged because Gift of Life uses her own Health
Weak while Dragonqueen is on cooldown
Healing reduction from enemy healers (Deckard Emerald, Ana Biotic Grenade) cuts her deeply
No escape and almost no mobility

good_into.why: Abundance and Preservation heal a percent of maximum Health to everyone in the circle, and Overprotective turns that into a shield, so long chip damage is undone cheaply without spending much Mana.

Wing Buffet knocks back and slows an arc of melee heroes and Dragonqueen halves the length of stuns, roots and slows on her, so she survives being collapsed on better than other healers while her team brawls.
Dragonqueen is on a long cooldown, so she wins the fight at a static objective when it is up (Infernal Shrines is the guide's best map). The team must hold the fight for when it is ready.
Her Mana use is low next to other healers and Gift of Life costs no Mana at all, so she outlasts long drawn out fights better than most.

bad_into.why: A diver who sticks to her interrupts the 1.25 second Dragonqueen channel and she has no mobility, no cleanse and no unstoppable. Gift of Life gets weaker as she takes damage.
Stuns and roots cancel Dragonqueen and Cleansing Flame casts, and she has only Dragon Scales (armor, once every 10 seconds) as a counter. A Cocoon or a Mighty Gust shuts down the whole fight.
Skillshots and area damage on the Abundance circle (Concussion Mine, Flamestrike) deny the delayed heal, and ranged heroes can hit her without ever being slowed or knocked back.
An assassin that reaches her before Dragonqueen is up kills a healer with 1308 damage taken per minute measured and no escape. Pacify at level 13 is her only peel.

Ana.strengths_note: Healing Dart, Sleep Dart and Nano Boost give burst healing and pick potential at range.
Ana.weaknesses_note: Very fragile and reliant on cooldowns.
Ana.owner_notes: Her anti heal grenade is a key tool.
wants: A mage or spell damage hero for Nano Boost (Jaina, Kael'thas, Li-Ming)
Reliable crowd control so Sleep Dart and Biotic Grenade always connect
A frontline that stays on a line so Healing Dart does not get blocked
Peel from the tank and a second backline body to stop divers
gives: Anti healing that denies enemy sustain and Heroic heals
A long range sleep that sets up a kill or breaks an engage
Nano Boost: 30% Spell Power and fast Basic Ability cooldowns for 8 seconds
Stun removal and armor with Smelling Salts
weak: No mobility and no real escape
Healing Dart misses cost a lot
Self heal depends on her being in range of a target
Sleep breaks on damage so it needs a team that waits
Weak into dive

good_into.why: Biotic Grenade on an enemy team gives 100% less healing for 1.75 seconds, and Anti-Healer makes it larger. She is a hard counter to a team that relies on one big healer or Heroic heals.
Grenade covers the whole group a Brightwing, Lucio or Malfurion style healer is feeding, so one throw shuts the team's healing for the window your team uses to burst.

Night Terrors deals 8% of maximum Health on waking, Shrike Doses chip big targets and Sleep Dart removes an engaging tank for 3 seconds. All of it is percent based or timing based, so tanks gain nothing from extra Health.
Sleep Dart on a diving melee hero is the best answer, Debilitating Dart halves a diver's damage, and Smelling Salts removes the stun that melee burst combos rely on.
Smelling Salts removes a stun and adds 50 Armor, and Purifying Darts removes roots and slows, so stun then burst compositions lose their main plan.

bad_into.why: She has no mobility and no self peel except Sleep Dart and Debilitating Dart, so divers like Zeratul or Chen who reach her backline remove her before she can heal. She is the first target.

Her darts are skillshots with travel time, her healing comes in small chunks and her only protection is a sleep that breaks on any damage. One assassin reaching her removes the healer and the Nano Boost target's value.
Healing Dart cannot be self cast and misses fast allies, and Sleep Dart is a skillshot that mobile heroes dodge. Mobile divers also decide where the fight takes place.
Long range poke on a stationary Ana in Aim Down Sights or Eye of Horus hits an unprotected backline and she cannot retreat. The guide names Hanzo style poke as a decent counter.

Anduin.strengths_note: Leap of Faith, Lightbomb and Divine Star give a strong pull and heal.
wants: A tank with a stun, root or slow so Chastise always lands
Heroes who can use a Lightbomb (Thrall, Muradin, Sylvanas with mobility)
Peel in front of him, since he has no mobility
Allies who lack escapes (Diablo, Raynor) to use Leap of Faith on
gives: Leap of Faith, one of the best save abilities in the game
Burst healing for focused targets
Lightbomb engage or follow up stun
A baseline cleanse and Protected in the Heroic
weak: No mobility and stands still to heal
Low area healing
Leap of Faith only helps one ally every 70 seconds
Measured win rate of 0.473 across 3667 games is below even

good_into.why: Leap of Faith pulls the target out and makes him Unstoppable for the travel, which denies one target burst, and Desperate Prayer or Holy Word: Salvation give an instant answer to a combo. The guide calls him a strong choice against comps that burst one hero.
Chastise roots the first hero in a line and Lightbomb stuns a clump that reaches the target, so melee heroes that walk up get a hard stop. Censure adds a stun to Chastise.
Chastise as a follow up to a tank's engage and a Lightbomb on an engaging ally leave an enemy backline with little time to react.
Leap of Faith and Holy Word: Salvation answer a focused combo, but only on one ally at a time and only if he is not the target himself. Better against dive on his allies than dive on him.

bad_into.why: Area healing is low and Lightwell only heals one target every few seconds, so a team that chips five targets all fight long drains him. Renew and Divine Star help but do not scale with groups.
Chastise is a slow projectile that mobile heroes dodge and Lightbomb has a 1.5 second fuse, so his CC is easy to avoid and he cannot catch them.
Stuns and roots cancel the Holy Word: Salvation channel and Flash Heal, and he has no escape himself. Chained CC on him ends his usefulness, and Leap of Faith cannot target himself.
He channels Flash Heal standing still with no mobility, so a diver like Sonya or Zeratul who reaches him leaves Leap of Faith as the only answer and it is for one ally.

Anub'arak.strengths_note: Burrow Charge into Cocoon or Impale gives a reliable engage and a strong pick.
Anub'arak.weaknesses_note: Low damage and thin sustain mean he needs allies ready to follow his initiation.

extra.objective_notes: Burrow scouts and rotates but he soaks poorly

wants: Burst damage that follows Impale and Cocoon within 2 seconds
A second source of crowd control or a mobile assassin for the follow up
A healer that can heal through spell damage poke
Teammates that hold position near him so Burrow Charge does not overextend
gives: Long range stun to interrupt channels and start fights
Cocoon to delete a key hero or split a rotating team
Scouting and vision from Burrow Charge and Beetles
Spell armor and skillshot blocking with Beetles
weak: Fragile for a tank, measured damage taken is very high at 3345 per minute with a small health pool
Low waveclear and siege
Every main ability is a skillshot that can be avoided
Burrow Charge is the only escape, so a failed dive is a death

good_into.why: Long range Impale and Burrow Charge interrupt channels, and Cocoon removes one backline hero for 7 seconds so the team collapses on the rest.
Heroes without a dash cannot dodge the slow Impale spike once Burrow Charge or Bed of Barbs slows them, and they cannot leave a Cocoon follow up.
Harden Carapace with Nerubian Armor and Chitinous Plating gives large spell armor on a 7 second cooldown, and Subterranean Shield absorbs chip while closing the gap.
Cocoon makes the caster untargetable and unable to act, so it can be used to deny a channelled or global heroic by isolating the hero.
Beetles tank structure and mercenary shots, and Alterac Pass play with Scarab Host captures the objective alone.

bad_into.why: Anub'arak has a small health pool for a tank and Nerubian Armor and Harden Carapace do nothing against basic attack physical damage, so melee auto attackers focus him down.
Assassins that dash on him ignore the spike skillshots and kill through a low health pool. Locust Swarm is barely useful against burst.
Long range skillshots are avoided by kiters and his own damage is too low to punish a mobile ranged hero.
His damage is small hits from Beetles and Burning Beetles that sustain healers undo, and Debilitation is the only answer for a big healer.
Burrow Charge is his only escape and Cocoon can be broken fast by enemy attacks, so heavy crowd control after he commits punishes the dive.

Artanis.strengths_note: Blade Dash and Phase Prism let him dive and Shield Overload keeps him alive.
Artanis.weaknesses_note: Melee and weak to CC and kiting.
wants: Crowd control to hold targets in melee range after Blade Dash plus Phase Prism
A sustained healer such as Malfurion to refill health between shields
Mobility buffs or engages, as he lacks his own
gives: Suppression Pulse blind that cuts enemy auto damage across the whole map
Phase Prism swap to pull a target or peel a diver
Long fight durability that holds a lane or front line
Unlimited range heroics that join fights from anywhere
weak: Almost no mobility
Blind and crowd control shut off Shield Overload
Weak to kiting and burst
Measured win rate and damage are below league norms

good_into.why: Shield Overload refreshes off autos and Blade Dash hits, so he wins long melee brawls where he stays in range and keeps swinging.
Shield Overload triggers below 75 percent health and Shield Battery recharges it fast while the shield is up, so chip damage is largely absorbed.
Phase Prism swaps him onto a backline hero and grants Unstoppable, and Titan Killer with Twin Blades gives percent health burst on mobile targets.
Plasma Burn damages structures while Shield Overload is active, and Amateur Opponent plus Blade Dash clear camps and summons well.

bad_into.why: Blind stops his auto loop and his only gap closer is Twin Blades. Roots, slows, knockbacks (E.T.C. Face Melt) and stuns cancel Blade Dash animation and leave him stranded.
He has almost no mobility and no ranged damage, so a kiting hero never lets him land the autos that power Shield Overload.
Shield Overload needs him to take damage and be below 75 percent, and a burst combo kills him before the shield and cooldown loop starts.
Heavily armored targets soak his physical autos, and he cannot reach their backline without Phase Prism or Twin Blades.

Arthas.strengths_note: Frozen Tempest and Death Coil give heavy self sustain, wave clear and lane control.
Arthas.weaknesses_note: Little engage and he is easy to kite or root down.

extra.objective_notes: Strong solo laner who pushes towers well

wants: Damage and crowd control that follow Howling Blast roots
A healer that does not need to stand in front
Heroes with mobility or speed buffs for him, such as Zarya Speed Barrier
Ranged support that covers the enemy kiters he cannot reach
gives: Roots and attack speed slows that shut down melee heroes
A durable frontline with strong self sustain
Summon Sindragosa structure disable for pushes and dives
Armor shred with Shattered Armor for burst
weak: No mobility
Mana hungry Frozen Tempest
Weak to displacement, healing reduction and burst mages
Cannot interrupt casts

good_into.why: Frozen Tempest slows movement and attack speed up to 40 percent, Howling Blast roots, and Rime blocks auto attacks. The guide calls him a shutdown for low mobility melee heroes.
Remorseless Winter roots anything that stays in Frozen Tempest and heals him, and Absolute Zero roots for 2.5 seconds then slows.
Summon Sindragosa disables enemy structures, minions and mercenaries for 20 seconds, which makes pushes and dives safe.
Icebound Fortitude, Rime blocks and Anti-Magic Shell give armor and spell immunity, and self cast Death Coil with Immortal Coil heals him back up through a dive.
Rune Tap, Army of the Dead sacrifices and Death Coil keep him standing in long fights where a high health frontline is the target.

bad_into.why: Ranged heroes that kite stay outside the 3.5 range of Frozen Tempest and Howling Blast is slow, so he cannot apply the slows that define him.
High mobility assassins such as Zeratul step out of Howling Blast and Frozen Tempest, and he has no mobility until Path of Frost at level 20.
He cannot interrupt enemy casts, and displacement such as Wrecking Ball pulls him out of position with no way to answer except Icebound Fortitude.
Frozen Tempest drains his mana quickly at 13 per second, and long range mages burst him before he reaches them (Jaina, Kel'Thuzad per the guide).
Several ranged damage dealers out of his reach means his slows and roots do little while healing reduction cancels Death Coil and Ghoul sacrifices.

Auriel.strengths_note: Crystal Aegis, Ray of Heaven and Resurrect offer excellent sustain.
Auriel.weaknesses_note: Low damage and slow to protect herself.
Auriel.owner_notes: Needs to damage people, or a teammate with her trait on has to deal damage, to fill her heals. Decent damage and sustain heal in some comps and weak in others. No solid escape.
wants: A sustained ranged damage dealer to carry Bestow Hope (Valla, Hanzo, Raynor, Lunara)
Heroes who can push enemies into walls or create terrain (Diablo, Nazeebo)
A flanker or double soaker so she can focus a side lane
An engaging frontline, because she has no engage herself
gives: Large area healing that grows with team damage
Strong peel: knockback, stun into terrain, blind, stasis
Wave clear and no Mana trouble, so good early on Braxis style maps
Resurrect to turn a lost trade into an even one
weak: Healing is weak out of combat
No mobility and no cleanse
Poke and burst both break her
Her Heroic abilities telegraph the target and can be followed up on

good_into.why: Detainment Strike knocks a diver off and Blinding Flash on the center of Sacred Sweep blinds melee auto attackers for 2 seconds. Heavy Burden slows them. Melee heroes stay in range of her Sweep and fill her Energy.
Knockback with stun on terrain, Crystal Aegis stasis for 2 seconds and Piercing Lash peel an assassin well. She is better at peeling than most healers but cannot cleanse a stun on an ally.
Detainment Strike into terrain stuns and Converging Force pulls heroes into the Sweep center for a 160 hit, so slow heroes take burst damage from her while she fills Energy.
Bestow Hope converts damage into Energy, and fights into tanks are long and give her the most hits on Heroes. Healing then scales with the whole team's damage done, not with her own mana pool.

bad_into.why: Her Energy comes from damage dealt, so a team that out pokes hers leaves her with no Energy to heal with. The guide says she does not do well against poke, especially when behind.
Ray of Heaven has a 4 second cooldown and cannot undo burst, and she has no mobility, no cleanse and no unstoppable. Diving onto Auriel stops all her healing at once.
Her Heroic abilities leave the target exploitable (Crystal Aegis stasis is easy to follow up on, Resurrect is a long channel) and a chain stun on the Bestow Hope ally cuts her Energy flow.
Detainment Strike and Sacred Sweep need the enemy near or against terrain, and kiters that stay out of range make her damage (and Energy) low.

Azmodan.strengths_note: Globe of Annihilation and Demonic Invasion give elite structure damage and wave clear.
Azmodan.weaknesses_note: Zero mobility and an easy target.
Azmodan.owner_notes: A burst ranged damage hero who sieges structures well. Cooldown dependent: big burst, then not much damage. No escapes.
wants: Reliable area crowd control so Globe and All Shall Burn land uninterrupted
Teammates who leave minion waves for him to stack Annihilation on
A frontline that stops dives and body blocks assassins
Healer that keeps him alive while channeling, since he has little self sustain
gives: Huge siege damage and fast wave and camp clear from range
Global lane pressure with Demon Lieutenant and late Inescapable Annihilation
Area damage in long fights from stacked Globe and Tide of Sin
A large health pool that makes him hard to pick off for a ranged assassin
weak: Very vulnerable to interruption on both main abilities
Weak early because Annihilation has to be stacked
No escape and a big hitbox that is easy to hit and body block
Little teamfight utility beyond damage, and no hard crowd control of his own

good_into.why: Globe of Annihilation is slow and telegraphed, and All Shall Burn needs an uninterrupted 2.5 second channel. Targets that cannot sidestep or interrupt take the full hit, and Sin's Grasp slows them for the final burst.

Melee heroes have to walk into Globe range and clump on objectives. Demon Warriors with Brutish Vanguard slow attackers by 30 percent, and Trample is a short gap closer into Genji or Zeratul style assassins.
All Shall Burn plus a Globe is big burst on a single target, and Globe chip is hard to undo for a healer without area or sustained healing.
Demon Lieutenant has global cast range and Inescapable Annihilation makes Globe global, so Azmodan answers side lanes and snipes structures from anywhere.
Demonic Invasion with Siegebreaker plus Globe stacks can take a Fort in one cast, so against comps that lean on towers and walls he outsieges them.

bad_into.why: Globe of Annihilation and All Shall Burn go on full cooldown when interrupted, and he has no Unstoppable, so stuns, silences and knockbacks turn his channels into nothing.
Large hitbox, slow movement, no escape except the Trample talent. Divers body block and kill him before Demon Warriors matter.
Assassins with a gap closer reach him inside his minimum useful range, and All Shall Burn slows his own movement by 30 percent while channeling.
Globe is slow with a long travel time, so Tracer, Genji, Lunara and similar heroes dodge it and kite his channels.

Blaze.strengths_note: Flame Stream, Oil Spill and Bunker Drop give strong lane pressure from the offlane.
Blaze.weaknesses_note: Very short range and low sustain make him easy to kite and burst.

extra.objective_notes: Pushes a lane to force rotations

Blaze.owner_notes: Blaze plays as a bruiser (offlaner), not a tank.
wants: A partner to start the engage because Jet Propulsion is slow
Skillshot heroes that use Oil Spill slows and Jet Propulsion stuns
A healer or mage that handles poke while he soaks
Damage that finishes kills since his own single target output is low
gives: Elite waveclear, camp clear and siege
Bunker Drop to cancel heroics such as Temporal Loop
Slows that raise uptime for assassins and skillshot heroes
Spell power reduction with Suppressive Fire
weak: Immobile and easy to kite
Slow engage
Low single target damage
Percent based damage cuts through his large health pool and armor

good_into.why: Oil Spill slows 50 percent, Nanomachine Coating cuts attack speed 35 percent, Meltdown cuts damage, and cone autos with Pyromania hit every melee hero standing on him. The guide says he excels at disrupting aggressive melee heroes.
Bunker Drop clears most crowd control and damage over time effects and shields fragile allies, and Pyromania gives 40 armor on demand against single target dives.
Measured siege damage of 6404 per minute, Incinerator Gauntlets and Burn Notice make him one of the best pushers, and double soaking is his strength.
Juggernaut Plating converts spell damage into a shield and Endurance Stimpack shields burst, while Ignited Oil Spill heals him in sustained fights.
Flame Stream and Oil Spill hit predictable targets, Jet Propulsion has a long wind up and lands best on slowed or stunned heroes.

bad_into.why: Jet Propulsion has a 0.375 second delay, so mobile heroes such as Tracer dodge it, and he has no mobility besides it.
He relies on skillshots that can be avoided and is slow, so kiters outrange and outwalk his short cone.
Percent health damage and a large health pool matter against him, and his damage is too low to threaten heavy frontlines.
Limited burst and single target output means he does not kill the dive, and the guide lists percent based damage as his worst problem.
Ranged teams can stand outside his short cone and Oil Spill area, so his sustain and slows hit less.

Brightwing.strengths_note: Phase Shift and Blink Heal make her safe and mobile.
wants: High maximum Health allies so Phase Shift heals a lot
Dive allies who can follow her teleport (Genji, Tracer)
A frontline that can take the engage she cannot
A second healer or support so she can run Emerald Wind or damage talents
gives: Free healing with Soothing Mist, no Mana needed
A cleanse on a 75 second cooldown
Polymorph as pick or shutdown on one hero
Global presence and fast soak, which outnumbers fights
weak: Cannot use a mount
Healing is slow: ticks every 4 seconds and a 2 second teleport
Needs map awareness and good positioning
Weak against engages that ignore Polymorph
Measured win rate of 0.469 over 2766 games

good_into.why: Polymorph removes a diver's attacks for 1.5 seconds and shuts down mobile heroes like Zeratul or Genji, Emerald Wind knocks everyone off, and Pixie Dust gives 30 Spell Armor against mages and abilities.
Phase Shift lets her soak a lane alone and join the team anywhere, which is the best global presence in the game. She pressures lanes and arrives with a 25% heal.
Polymorph plus Sticky Flare or Hush! locks a mobile hero in place, and Soothing Mist cleanses slows and roots on her allies so dive and kite pressure does not stick.
Soothing Mist heals everyone every 4 seconds without Mana and Pixie Power gives 55 Spell Armor, so spread out chip damage and spell poke is healed cheaply.

bad_into.why: Anub'arak, Johanna and E.T.C. style engages are not stopped by Polymorph, and the cleanse is on a 75 second cooldown, so a chain of stuns and roots leaves her with little.
Her heals are on 4 second ticks and Phase Shift has a 2 second delay, so burst kills before healing lands. Phase Out is her only personal answer.
She needs to stay close to allies for Soothing Mist, so backline ranged damage that hits the group hits her too, and she cannot escape without Blink Heal.
She does not have a way to kill tanks: Polymorph on a tank needs Critterize to matter, and Soothing Mist is flat 110 healing per tick which is small on high Health targets.

Cassia.strengths_note: Lightning Fury, Ball Lightning and Valkyrie give flexible poke and good wave clear.
Cassia.weaknesses_note: Low defense and relies on energy and mana.
wants: Heroes that blind or slow so Blinding Light and Martial Law get bonus damage
A frontline that absorbs crowd control and lets her stay moving
A focused healer, since Avoidance armor multiplies healing received
Allied crowd control to set up Ball Lightning and Fend
gives: Consistent single target damage against tanks and bruisers
A strong answer to basic attack melee assassins and bruisers
Reasonable wave and camp clear with Fend
Interrupt of channelled Heroics with a low cooldown Valkyrie
weak: No escape, and crowd control removes her armor
Short range for an assassin
Very mana hungry
Dependent on level 13 and 16 talents for her real power

good_into.why: Blinding Light removes basic attacks of melee heroes, Surge of Light stores their damage and releases an area hit, and Avoidance armor reduces their hits while she keeps moving. Grounding Rod and Martial Law punish them further.
Blinding Light plus Fend and Ball Lightning let her win a duel against a diving assassin that relies on basic attacks, and Avoidance gives up to 30 armor against their physical damage.
Martial Law deals percent health damage (3 percent when slowed, stunned or blinded) and Titan's Revenge ignores armor, so she chews through tanks that other poke assassins cannot.
Her armor makes single target heals very efficient, and the guide notes her value jumps with a focused healer, so she is stronger when her own healer has this style.

bad_into.why: Avoidance armor only exists while she is moving, so any stun or root removes it within about a second. Fend can be cancelled early and she has no escape.
Her attack range is short, so longer range assassins and mages win trades in the open and punish her dive with Fend.
She has no good way to close from range with Fend on cooldown and very few ways to heal back chip except Inner Light and Plate of the Whale.
Blinding Light is a ground target area, so stealthed heroes avoid it, and her kit has no reveal.

Chen.strengths_note: Flying Kick, Breath of Fire and Storm, Earth, Fire give flexible utility and solid camp clear.
Chen.weaknesses_note: Hard to learn and vulnerable to heavy burst.

extra.objective_notes: Fine at camps and boss capture

wants: A frontline partner so he can duel in a lane safely
Peel against interrupts so he can channel Fortifying Brew
Follow up damage on Ignited targets
gives: Wandering Keg to knock enemies into the team or away from it
Storm, Earth, Fire for a sudden three body engage
Enough to Share shields for nearby allies
Strong solo lane that wins duels
weak: Low baseline wave clear
Conditional mobility, Flying Kick needs a target
Struggles against interrupts
Needs Brew management

good_into.why: Stagger prevents three seconds of damage then spreads 75 percent over five, and Fortifying Brew shields on top, so a burst combo is largely wasted on him.
He wins duels with Brew slow, Ignite and self healing, and Eye of the Tiger heals him off Brew soaked targets.
Fortifying Brew shields and Brewmaster's Balance regeneration absorb chip, and Flying Kick lets him close on a poke hero.
Keg Smash slows 40 percent after a moment, Pressure Point slows 80 percent, and Flying Kick plus Wandering Keg close distance.

bad_into.why: Stuns and silences stop Fortifying Brew channeling and Stagger timing, and the guide lists interrupts as his weakness.
The Ignite is a damage over time that strong healers undo, so his kill pressure drops.
Without percent health or armor reduction beyond the Accumulating Flame mythic reward, he cannot burst armored fronts.
Brew costs and a cone ability make him work to reach a ranged line that can kite his low baseline mobility.

Cho.strengths_note: Upheaval, Surging Fist and Hammer of Twilight set up and win close fights.
Cho.weaknesses_note: Two player hero that suffers when the pair is not coordinated.

extra.objective_notes: Cho and Gall together soak objectives well

Cho.owner_notes: Cho and Gall are one hero in game played by two players. Cho is the bruiser half.
wants: A dedicated single target healer such as Alexstrasza, Brightwing or Ana
A resilient bruiser with waveclear to cover macro
A teammate to play Gall and talk, plus a team that can play with only four bodies
No second assassin so the team is not too fragile
gives: A huge health pool frontline with a second ranged damage source
Long range sustain poke from Gall
Displacement and stuns from Hammer of Twilight and Upheaval
Vision from Eye of Kilrogg
weak: Weak early game, snowball maps punish him
Two heroes die with one death
Percent damage and stacked crowd control
Draft is easily countered and uses two draft slots

good_into.why: Huge health pool, Consuming Blaze heals per enemy ignited, Enraged Regeneration and Surging Dash sustain, and Twilight Veil armor make him durable against chip damage.
Gall's Dread Orb, Shadow Bolt Volley and Twisting Nether reach the backline from a safe tank body, and Upheaval pulls them into the team.
Hammer of Twilight pushes and stuns, Power Surge slows, and Twilight Veil armor blocks autos while Cho'gall out damages melee heroes with Gall behind him.
Power Surge slow and Surging Fist catch low mobility heroes, and Favor of the Old Gods roots with Upheaval, which the guide ties to Twisting Nether.
Enemy teams with no healing cannot punish with attrition, and Cho'gall scales into the strongest late game in the game, per the guide.

bad_into.why: Cocoon or Containment Disc turns the fight into a 5v3 because both halves are locked, and Surging Fist and Upheaval can be interrupted.
Percent damage such as Cursed Bullet, Last Rites and Seven Sided Strike ignores armor, and a death costs two heroes worth of experience.
He occupies two slots, so the team has four bodies and loses map presence and rotation, and he is weak in the early game.
Cho's melee body is hard to get on a kiter without C'Thun's Gift, and Gall alone is stationary.
Snowball maps and early objectives punish his weak early game and the four man team, as the guide says on Battlefield of Eternity and Warhead Junction.

Chromie.strengths_note: Dragon's Breath, Sand Blast and Temporal Loop give strong burst at range.
wants: A frontline of a tank and a bruiser that keeps divers off her
Allied crowd control or slows so Sand Blast and Dragon's Breath land
A healer with mana support such as Malfurion or Ana
Burst damage heroes who benefit from Time Troubles armor shred
gives: Long range burst and poke that wins objective fights from a safe distance
Early level 8 Heroic power spike because Timewalker gives talents two levels early
Slowing Sands choke point control or a Temporal Loop pick
Time Trap stasis that can protect an ally or stop a diver
weak: Low health pool and below average mobility
Needs accurate prediction of target movement for delayed shots
Weak solo lane and no sustain
Time Trap is slow to arm and Temporal Loop can be cleansed

good_into.why: Piercing Sands pierces clumped melee frontlines, Slowing Sands covers choke points, and Time Trap with Time Troubles strips armor from a diver. Melee heroes cannot reach her from range.
Sand Blast does 305 per hit with an Echo for 40 percent more, so squishy ranged heroes die in two or three hits at the longest range in the game.
The 0.5 second delay on Sand Blast and Dragon's Breath is a non issue for targets that cannot sidestep, and Mobius Loop slows them further.
Single target burst with Temporal Loop and A Proper Greeting kills the healer or carry before a low sustain healer can undo it.
Quantum Overdrive, Fast Forward and spammable Sand Blast let her out poke most other ranged assassins when she is safe behind a frontline.

bad_into.why: Low health, no mobility except Gnome Speed Ahead and a delayed Time Trap, so Tracer, Illidan or Zeratul style divers reach her and Time Out is her only escape.
Fast assassins are hard to hit with a delayed projectile and can punish any bad position.
Both main abilities have a delay, so mobile heroes dodge them.
A stun cancels her kiting and sets up a dive. Temporal Loop can also be cleansed with Unstoppable effects.
Very beefy targets absorb Sand Blast without dying, so she needs a team to focus them.

D.Va.strengths_note: Boosters and Defense Matrix give mobility and a huge effective health pool in the mech.
D.Va.weaknesses_note: Must rebuild the mech after losing it and is punished when caught out.
D.Va.owner_notes: A bruiser. Soaks lanes, controls points with her bombs, and disrupts fights with Bunny Hop.
wants: Damage dealers to turn her Defense Matrix and engage into kills
A healer to refill the mech between fights
Follow up on her Boosters knockback
gives: Defense Matrix damage reduction field for the whole team
Mobile engage and disengage with Boosters
Strong siege and wave clear
Bunny Hop or Micro Missiles as flexible heroics
weak: Mech and Pilot cooldown cycle leaves gaps
Low self healing
Blind and silence stop Defense Matrix tactics
Needs damage dealers to convert her setup

good_into.why: Defense Matrix reduces damage by 60 percent in an area and she gets a second life as a Pilot, so chip damage into her is wasted.
Defense Matrix blocks projectile and spell damage on the team, and Boosters closes the gap on backliners.
Very high siege damage, 50 percent Self Destruct against structures, and Micro Missiles and Bunny Hop strip towers.
Boosters knocks away, Bunny Hop stomps stun on the fourth hit, and Self Destruct kills clustered squishies.

bad_into.why: Mech health is a second pool but burst plus Pilot Mode leaves her without Defense Matrix and mobility for a 45 second Call Mech cooldown.
Stuns, silences and roots interrupt Boosters and Self Destruct timing, and Bunny Hop only grants Unstoppable on that heroic.
Her mech has no big self heal outside Liquid Cooling and Full Metal, so a team without healing cannot refill it across a long siege.
Fusion Cannons are physical close range chip and do little against heavy armor.

Deathwing.strengths_note: Cataclysm, Molten Flame and CC immunity make him a strong sieger and global presence.
Deathwing.weaknesses_note: Cannot be healed or shielded and has slow casting animations.

extra.objective_notes: Dragonflight gives global rotations and siege

Deathwing.owner_notes: A bruiser, often taken in the 4 man as a damage dealer. Pick him when the other team has no percent damage hero and when they have a pick comp: he cannot be stunned, so he wrecks those comps. A strong late pick in the right situations.
wants: A healer that heals without him (his own self healing carries him)
Teammates who can keep enemies grouped for Molten Flame
Vision and map objectives to time Dragonflight
gives: Huge teamfight damage and crowd control (stun, fear)
Global presence through Dragonflight
Armor reduction and damage reduction debuffs on enemies
Long term objective pressure with scorched ground
weak: Ignores ally healing and shields
Channeled Molten Flame is stationary and interruptible
Armor plates depend on health
Very complex to play

good_into.why: Molten Flame's doubled spell damage on heroes and armor plates melt even a bruiser front line, and Death Drop cuts their spell armor.
Damage is dense and front loaded, so healing cannot keep up with Molten Flame and the landing burst.
Onslaught slow, Bellowing Roar fear and Gaze Onto Destruction cut enemy damage by 75 percent in a fight, and he is Unstoppable so he is not locked down.
Permanent Unstoppable makes stuns, roots and slows irrelevant to him, and his own stun lock punishes their commitment.
Dragonflight is a global presence tool that joins fights anywhere and punishes split pushes and distant objectives.

bad_into.why: Molten Flame is a channel that roots him in place for the duration and Dragonflight has a long delay, so mobile ranged heroes can dodge it.
Armor plates fall every 25 percent health and he cannot be healed by allies, so a fast kill on him is the plan.
Without ally heals and with only Molten Blood and Draconic Might for sustain, he cannot out heal poke before landing.
His strongest damage needs him to be near them and the Dragonflight cooldown is long.

Deckard.strengths_note: Healing Potion, Horadric Cube and Lorenado offer steady sustain.
wants: Heroes who can follow up on his CC with burst damage
Low mobility melee allies who can pick up stocked potions
A tank with reliable CC that Scroll of Sealing can follow
Choke points and long objective fights
gives: Efficient single target healing that is nearly free in Mana
Area CC: Sleep, root, knockback
Healing reduction with Emerald
Potions that pre heal allies in other lanes or at objectives
weak: Weak against burst and dive
No cleanse and no unstoppable
Wants allies around him because Fortitude of the Faithful needs a hero near
Struggles against unstoppable and cleanse effects
No mobility

good_into.why: Emerald on Horadric Cube reduces enemy healing received by 75% for 4 seconds. Aim it at the kill target so the healer cannot save him. Perfect Gems shortens Gem cooldown to 5 seconds.
Lorenado knocks melee away and Kanai's Cube cuts their damage by 30%, Scroll of Sealing roots them after a slow, and Healing Potions on the ground feed low mobility allies who fight in a clump.
Scroll of Sealing is a slow telegraphed root, so heroes that cannot dodge it take 150 plus Stone Curse damage and a 1.5 second root. Sleep also locks them from far.
Stocked Healing Potions have no Mana cost per use that matters and Potion of Shielding adds a shield, so he out heals chip damage on single targets for the whole fight.
Sleep and Lorenado hold a frontline for the team, and Super Healing Potion heals 100% more on potions left alone. He fights long and slow fights where tanks stand in his zone.

bad_into.why: Guide: weak against burst damage and no escape. One target healing and a 0.5 second cast on potions cannot undo a combo, and he has 0 mobility.
Scroll of Sealing is a 2.25 second telegraph and Healing Potion misses moving allies, so mobile heroes slip his CC and dodge potions.
Horadric Cube and Scroll miss kiters that stay out of the cone, and he cannot close distance to enemy ranged heroes.
Ranged heroes outrange his zone and can engage him easily. Unstoppable and cleanse effects (Whitemane, Johanna) also ignore his CC.

Dehaka.strengths_note: Drag, Burrow and Essence Collection make him strong at stealing camps and soloing.
Dehaka.weaknesses_note: Weak wave clear and offers little peel.
Dehaka.owner_notes: A bruiser who clears waves and offlanes before the objective to pull the other offlaner away, then burrows into the objective with the team and turns a 4v4 into a 5v4 with his global. If the other offlaner does not contest him he keeps pushing while the team stalls, and it is better still when a camp is timed to push with him.
flex_roles: Offlaner who pulls the other offlaner away
wants: Follow up damage after his Drag
Vision of bush paths and objectives
A carry to benefit from the picks he sets up
gives: Pick potential with Drag and Isolation
Fast rotations and map presence
Healing reduction on the focus target
Camp clear and siege through Dark Swarm
weak: Low hero damage
Drag is cancelled by stun or silence
Needs Essence to keep sustain up
Depends on teammates to capitalise on picks

good_into.why: Drag stuns and pulls a backliner out of position, and Isolation silences and blinds one target for a pick.
Paralyzing Enzymes cuts healing received by 50 percent on the dragged target and Drag can pull the healer away from his team.
Brushstalker and Burrow give mobility, Drag grabs a retreating hero, and Isolation slows.
Brushstalker is a stealthed global style travel tool, so he gets to fights and objectives across the map quickly.
Burrow is invulnerable for 2 seconds and Adaptation heals the damage taken over 4 seconds.

bad_into.why: Silence or stun during Drag cancels it, and Adaptation and Burrow are his only dodge tools.
Low hero damage output and a drag that cannot move heavy targets far make him poor at breaking a front line.
He has to walk into the poke and lacks a long range answer, though Essence healing helps.
Dark Swarm and Drag do not generate enough sustained pressure to overcome wide healing.

Diablo.strengths_note: Shadow Charge, Overpower and Apocalypse give strong single target and team engages.
Diablo.weaknesses_note: Little peel and his engage tools are predictable single targets.

extra.objective_notes: Fine soak but not a siege tank

Diablo.owner_notes: A tank who is built to catch people and get kills, not only to hold the front line.
wants: Burst damage and crowd control that follow Shadow Charge and Overpower
Heroic abilities that combo with Apocalypse
Maps with walls and choke points
Someone to cover waveclear and early game
gives: One of the best engages in the game
Body blocking and peel with Overpower
Interrupts channels with Shadow Charge stun
Lightning Breath zoning and objective control
weak: Weak early game before Souls and level 7
Low waveclear and siege
Conditional mobility, needs terrain
Percent health damage and kiting

good_into.why: Shadow Charge into Overpower reaches any hero, and the guide says he counters comps that rely on one key damage dealer or healer.
Apocalypse with Shadow Charge locks a single target, and Lightning Breath slows up to 40 percent so low mobility heroes cannot leave.
Lightning Breath makes him Unstoppable, Soul Shield gives spell armor, and Hellgate teleports out. The heroic can also dodge Chromie style heroics.
Diablo can pull the one healer away from the fight and stun them with Apocalypse, and Debilitating Flames halves the damage of slowed heroes.
Fire Stomp with Souls to the Flame and Black Soulstone health bonus heal through chip damage, and Soul Shield and Devil's Due raise sustain.

bad_into.why: He needs impassable terrain behind a target and melee range, and kiters such as Tychus counter him per the guide.
Early game is weak before 100 Souls and level 7, and a death without Black Soulstone leaves a large health pool dead.
Heroes that blink away from Shadow Charge or dodge Overpower waste his engage, and some can stop the animation (Penetrating Round).
Low waveclear and siege means he cannot answer split pushing or hold lanes, and he is weak on wide maps.
Fire Stomp and Lightning Breath damage is small enough that large AoE healers outheal it, while percent based damage kills his large health pool.

E.T.C..strengths_note: Mosh Pit and Powerslide give a wide engage, Stage Dive adds global reach.
E.T.C..weaknesses_note: Must stay in melee range and has weak sustain without allies.
wants: Heroes that follow up on Powerslide stun with skillshots
A healer that can grant Unstoppable during Mosh Pit such as Kharazim
A second tank who can solo lane if he plays offlane with Stage Dive
Burst damage because he lacks his own
gives: Engage from medium range
Interrupts through Face Melt knockback and daze
Power of the Horde shields and Speed Metal movement speed
Global presence at level 10 with Stage Dive
weak: Low damage output
Not as durable as most tanks
Low waveclear
Mosh Pit is easily interrupted

good_into.why: Face Melt knockback creates a buffer zone, Loud Speakers and Mic Check make it repeatable, and the guide says it helps against melee heroes without mobility such as Artanis.
Powerslide stun from a flank and Mosh Pit lock a backline in place, and Ride the Lightning extends reach.
Powerslide plus Mosh Pit for 4 seconds with no escape, since Powerslide stun lets him channel fully.
Face Melt dazes so they cannot dodge Powerslide, and Power of the Horde shields allies against burst while Face Melt keeps melee assassins off the backline.
Stage Dive and Ride the Lightning give global presence from level 10, so he joins objectives from anywhere on big maps.

bad_into.why: Ranged heroes with interrupts such as Li-Ming Wave of Force cancel Mosh Pit, and kiters stay out of Powerslide range.
Any stun, silence or knockback interrupts Mosh Pit and cancels Powerslide in a pinch, and he is not especially durable.
Below average durability for a tank, and Powerslide is both his engage and his escape, so a failed commit is a death.
Many ranged heroes with mobility are hard to catch and make Mosh Pit hard to land, per the guide.
He has little to answer or interrupt channels from range, and Stage Dive and Mosh Pit have long wind ups that can be interrupted or dodged.

Falstad.strengths_note: Flight and Hammerang give global map pressure and fast rotations.
Falstad.weaknesses_note: Mana hungry and caught by CC.
Falstad.owner_notes: A sustain damage hero with a global trait. Side lanes and stacks the level 1 auto quest. With stacks he does a lot of damage and gets a late game percent damage auto trait. Can go W but gets caught when the enemy has CC to punish it, or Q for poke damage.
wants: A frontline tank that draws attention and provides follow up crowd control
Shields or peel because his health pool is small
Poke or mage damage to use BOOMerang spell armor shred
A team that can hold the objective while he soaks side lanes
gives: Global rotation and soak that gives an experience lead
Mighty Gust for disengage, objective control, boss steals and anti dive
Decent wave and camp clear from range
Percent health damage against armoured frontlines in the basic attack build
weak: Needs very good positioning
Mediocre damage in the early game
Vulnerable to crowd control and gap closers
Barrel Roll is his only mobility besides a long cooldown Flight

good_into.why: Mighty Gust is a 60 second area knockback with a slow that splits a dive from its target. The guide calls him an excellent counterpick to dive comps, and Flight makes him Unstoppable for a moment.
Flight is a global with a 75 second cooldown, so he soaks lanes and joins fights, and he can answer side lane pressure.
Mighty Gust (and Wind Tunnel at level 20) pushes enemies off capture points, can steal boss camps, and Flight rotates quickly to objectives.
Hammerang slows and Mighty Gust keeps melee heroes from reaching the backline, and Lightning Rod punishes them for trying to run.
The guide specifically calls out Kharazim and Uther as healers who rely on positioning, which Mighty Gust ruins.

bad_into.why: Frail, and when Barrel Roll and Mighty Gust are spent, a high damage assassin with a gap closer kills him. The guide says to stay near the healer against such heroes.
Crowd control stops both Barrel Roll and Flight (Flight can be interrupted during its channel). He relies on mobility to survive.
He cannot safely stand near the objective against long range poke, and his early damage is mediocre.
No reveal in his kit and he relies on range and positioning.

Fenix.strengths_note: Weapon Modes, Shield Capacitor and Planet Cracker give strong sustained damage.
Fenix.weaknesses_note: Hard to reposition and has no peel.
Fenix.owner_notes: A medium range sustain damage hero. Can solo like Raynor but is often in a 3 or 4 man, where he catches waves and ganks like Sylvanas, Raynor or Greymane.
wants: Heroes that pull or clump enemies together such as Johanna or Diablo
Slows on the whole enemy team for Purification Salvo
A frontline that stops dives while he trades from range
Burst healing like Uther if he takes Rapid Recharge
gives: Strong solo lane and fast wave and camp clear
Sustained area damage and siege from range
Plasma Cutter slow that helps teammates land skillshots
Safe poking trades thanks to Shield Capacitor
weak: Large hitbox, easy to hit with skillshots
Must retreat to recharge shields, healers cannot refill the base shield
Warp is a channel that can be interrupted
No hard crowd control

good_into.why: Shield Capacitor regenerates 10 percent per second after 5 seconds without damage (Rapid Recharge cuts that to 3), so chip damage is wasted against him, and Phase Bomb out ranges many short range pokers.
Plasma Cutter slows melee heroes and Target Acquired gives him speed, so he kites them while splashing the group.
Phase Bomb splash and Plasma Cutter clear minions, mercenaries and summons very fast from range.
Offensive Cadence deals 6 percent max health on every third Repeater Cannon attack, and Photonic Weaponry adds 20 percent damage while shielded.
Splash with a slow and Purification Salvo (50 percent more to slowed targets) punishes grouped backline heroes if he is not interrupted.

bad_into.why: He has no hard crowd control and Warp is a channel that stuns and knockbacks cancel. The guide names E.T.C. and Lucio.
Assassins such as Zeratul and Genji follow Warp and are hard to peel, and large hitbox makes him easy to hit.
Divers burst through the shield. Divert Power drains the shield afterward and Warp is the only escape.
Other long range heroes out poke him when his shield is down, and his shield has to recharge out of combat so he loses the trade over a long skirmish.

Gall.strengths_note: Shadowflame and Dread Orb add strong ranged burst and wave clear to Cho.
Gall.weaknesses_note: Weak without a competent Cho and has no mobility.
Gall.owner_notes: Gall is the ranged assassin half of Cho and Gall.
wants: A dedicated healer, ideally strong single target healing
A real tank or bruiser, since Cho is a tank in name only
Teammates who play safely until levels 13, 16 and 20
A coordinated Cho partner on voice
gives: Huge area damage and structure damage with Dread Orb and Twilight Nova
A very large health pool and a strong late game
Area slow with Twisting Nether and stuns with Leaden Orb
Map vision with Eye of Kilrogg
weak: Weak early game
Counts as two heroes, so deaths cost double and the team is down a body
Vulnerable to percent health damage and to single target crowd control on Cho
Easily counter picked and has to be drafted last

good_into.why: Shadow Bolt Volley does 20 bolts of 87 at one target, Searing Shadows adds 2 percent of max health per Shadowflame, and Twisting Nether slows them. A comp of tanks that cannot burst him is walked down in long fights.
Twisting Nether slows nearby enemies by 50 percent, Leaden Orb stuns clumped melee heroes, and Cho's own Upheaval and Consuming Blaze combine with Gall's area damage.
Dread Orb and Runic Blast are telegraphed area hits and Dread Orb bounces several times on large targets. Immobile heroes take all three bounces.
Cho'gall scales into the strongest late game and a sustain comp gives time to reach level 16 and 20 without early deaths.

bad_into.why: Cho dying kills both heroes and gives two kills of experience, and Gall has Shove only to escape. Dive comps that can burst Cho before Ogre Hide matters are his worst case.
Gall is immune to stun and silence, but Cho is not. Anub'arak's Cocoon or Maiev's Containment Disc turn the fight into a 5 versus 3.
He is weak early and has to reach level 13 to 20 to be strong, and a comp that pokes and snowballs experience beats him before talents come online.
Single target damage and percent health damage (Cursed Bullet, Alpha Killer style) go through his large health pool, and Cho's lack of peel makes him easy to pick.

Garrosh.strengths_note: Wrecking Ball and Decimate dive the backline and Armor Up makes him durable.
Garrosh.weaknesses_note: No wave clear and no mobility outside his combo.
Garrosh.owner_notes: A tank who is built to catch people and get kills, not only to hold the front line.
wants: Burst damage and crowd control that follow Wrecking Ball
A secondary ranged engage such as Hanzo Dragon's Arrow
Mobility for him, for example Zarya Speed Barrier
Heroes that need an isolated target to kill
gives: A very hard to kill frontline from Armor Up
Displacement and taunt to start or break fights
Into the Fray to rescue allies and give Unstoppable
Spell power and healing reduction
weak: No mobility
Easily kited by ranged assassins
Low damage output and siege
Armor based, weak to percent damage

good_into.why: Wrecking Ball throws the closest hero on the spot or into the team, Earthshaker and Titanic Might isolate a target, and Warlord's Challenge silences and taunts a backline for 2 seconds.
Armor Up and Double Up make him very durable against autos, Intimidation cuts attack speed 30 percent, and Warlord's Challenge pulls melee heroes onto him.
Armor Up gives about half damage reduction at low health, Defensive Measures shields him and Into the Fray peels dived allies and gives them Unstoppable.
Body Check applies healing reduction for burst healers such as Whitemane or Brightwing, and Oppressor lowers healing from abilities.
Indomitable gives 1.5 seconds Unstoppable and Warlord's Challenge silences channels, so he can interrupt Mosh Pit or Drain Life.

bad_into.why: No mobility and no gap closer, so ranged assassins such as Lunara kite him away from the team.
He has to walk to targets and Wrecking Ball needs a hero within 2.25 range, so ranged teams outrange his engage.
Percent based damage and armor reduction (Leoric, Sylvanas Overwhelming Affliction) bypass Armor Up, and he has little damage himself.
Unstoppable heroes such as Johanna are skipped by Wrecking Ball, which then picks the second closest, and mobile heroes avoid Groundbreaker.
His damage is low and slows are short, so large AoE healers sustain through his poor output.

Gazlowe.strengths_note: Deth Lazor and Xplodium Charge give elite wave and structure damage.
Gazlowe.weaknesses_note: Fragile and offers little team fight impact.
wants: Peel and a frontline to protect him while turrets build
Wave control time so scrap accumulates
Teammates to follow Grav-O-Bomb
gives: Siege and objective push with turrets
Grav-O-Bomb 3000 pull and stun as an engage tool
Solo lane that frees teammates to rotate
Map control through turret zoning
weak: Scrap management
Low mobility
Low team fight value without turrets
Squishy to dives

good_into.why: Turrets and scrap fed Rock-It! Turrets plus Xplodium Charge give some of the highest siege damage in the game.
Hyperfocus Coils and Overklock add maximum health percent damage to Deth Lazor, Xplodium and autos.
He can hold a lane alone with turrets and wave clear, and wins solo lane against many heroes.
Master Blaster slows, turrets and EZ-PZ Dimensional Ripper cut incoming damage and Grav-O-Bomb 3000 stuns clumped melee heroes.

bad_into.why: Low mobility and health, and Grav-O-Bomb is his only strong crowd control, so a dive kills him before turrets matter.
Skillshot damage is easily dodged by mobile targets and he cannot catch them.
Turrets and Deth Lazor need vision of a target and have no detection.
Assassins can ignore turrets and kill him directly while he is fragile.

Gazlowe.owner_notes: A bruiser who plays the offlane. He does some ranged damage with turrets and Deth Lazor, but he is not a ranged damage dealer like Li-Ming, Valla, Raynor or Kael'thas.

Genji.strengths_note: Swift Strike and Deflect make him a high skill duelist.
Genji.weaknesses_note: Very difficult to play and easy to punish.
Genji.owner_notes: A dive burst assassin who bursts down a vulnerable backline. Escapes well, but is susceptible to CC and has low health.
wants: Burst damage and crowd control that lets him finish a single target (Jaina, Kael'thas)
A burst healer that gives armor or invulnerability like Uther
Crowd control already used by the enemy before he commits
Tank frontline that pulls enemy attention and cooldowns
gives: Backline pick potential and execute resets
Deflect that shuts down channelled or fast attacks of the enemy
Mobility to cross walls and flank
Takedowns from a single dive
weak: Weak wave clear and siege
Low health and needs constant healing
Very mana hungry
High skill floor, needs enemy crowd control to be spent

good_into.why: Swift Strike, Cyber Agility and Dragonblade reach a squishy ranged hero in seconds, and a kill resets Swift Strike so he can chain into the next target.
Teams full of ranged heroes have little to peel him, and Deflect blocks and returns their damage while he dives.
Targets that cannot dodge Swift Strike or Dragonblade are dead, and X-Strike has maximum damage on a stunned or rooted target.
Deflect blocks a large share of poke damage for 1.25 seconds and Augmented Guard turns it into a shield, then he dives the poker.

bad_into.why: Stun, root or silence takes away both Swift Strike and Cyber Agility, and he has no Unstoppable. The guide names Varian's Taunt and Malfurion's Twilight Dream.
Mobile ranged assassins like Lunara can bait him into overextending and poison keeps ticking through Deflect.
Point and click crowd control from heroes such as Uther cancels a dive on a backline target, and a burst healer undoes a failed kill.
Low health pool and Deflect with a 16 second cooldown means a faster assassin with burst can kill him in return.

Greymane.strengths_note: Worgen and Human forms with Darkflight give flexibility and pick potential.
Greymane.weaknesses_note: Complicated and punished when forms are mistimed.
wants: Crowd control and slows to turn on Lord of His Pack and Cursed Bullet
A strong initiator and frontline to open windows for the dive
A healer, since he cannot heal himself
Teammates who poke targets under 50 percent health first
gives: Outstanding single target damage and fast camp clear
Burst against tanks with Cursed Bullet
Flexible human and Worgen forms that suit most comps
Strong objective damage against bosses and structures
weak: No utility, crowd control or healing beyond damage
Low survivability, weak when playing from behind
Telegraphed playstyle and vulnerable to blinds and attack speed slows
Worgen builds need to commit in melee range

good_into.why: Cursed Bullet deals 35 percent of current health, so it is best on tanks at full health, and Alpha Killer adds 3 percent max health per Worgen attack.
The guide says he does well against comps full of mages, who are weak to a melee dive. Darkflight and Go for the Throat close the gap.
Gilnean Cocktail then Darkflight then Go for the Throat kills a squishy target in a burst, and Go for the Throat resets on a kill.
Basic attacks cleave with Tooth and Claw and splash with Hunter's Blunderbuss, and he gets camps and summons down quickly.

bad_into.why: He has no hard crowd control and no sustain, and stuns, roots, blinds or attack speed debuffs cripple a basic attack hero in Worgen form.
He has no defensive ability except Eyes in the Dark and Disengage, and faster burst heroes kill him in return.
Low survivability and no self healing, so a dive comp can kill him before Worgen burst.
Kiters poke him in Human form with longer range and can be hard to commit on if Darkflight is down.

Gul'dan.strengths_note: Life Tap, Fel Flame and Rain of Destruction give siege and burst.
Gul'dan.weaknesses_note: Zero mobility and risk from spending health.
wants: a sturdy frontline that peels and lets him sit at medium range
a healer to top him off after Life Tap
crowd control so Corruption and Drain Life are not walked out of
someone to deal with fast assassins that jump him
gives: fast wave clear that frees teammates to rotate
Horrify to split or defend with a two second fear and silence
high siege damage and team wide area damage from Corruption
self sufficient lane presence with Drain Life and Consume Soul
weak: no escape until the level 20 Demonic Circle
Life Tap health cost forces health and mana to be managed together

Frag Launcher range and Steel Trap zone enemies off channeled objectives such as Altars, Nukes and Tributes, which Icy Veins lists directly.

Barbed Chains armor reduction and Strip Shields (extra damage to shields) let him pull a tank apart or pull a squishy past one.

Nature's Toxin prevents stealthed heroes such as Nova, Valeera or Zeratul from re stealthing, and Natural Perspective reveals them for its duration.
Invigorating Spores deals 1.5 percent of maximum health per attack on a 3 stack target, and Unfair Advantage amplifies poison on slowed tanks.

bad_into.why: Heavy healing shuts down damage over time, so Malfurion or Stukov heal the poison almost as fast as she applies it.
Area heals touch every poisoned hero at once, so the spread out dot is wasted; Icy Veins names Malfurion and Stukov as her counters.
Illidan and Genji chase her down even after Leaping Strike, and she has no real burst of her own to stop them.
Her damage is slow and builds over time, so a fast dive kills her before the poison does anything.
Her mobility is her defense, and Galloping Gait or Leaping Strike do not help if she is stunned or rooted.

Lúcio.strengths_note: Amp It Up, Crossfade and Sound Barrier give team speed and area heals.
Lúcio.owner_notes: A good healer without great healing numbers but solid sustain. Can pick the shield heroic against burst or High Five to cleanse CC. High skill floor and ceiling. Played well he disrupts rotations and is hard to kill thanks to mobility, but heroes like Diablo can stun him on walls while he is wall riding.
wants: Low mobility Heroes who benefit from speed
Melee or dive Heroes to enable
Wave clear from elsewhere
A tank who stays close so the aura reaches
gives: Constant AoE healing aura
Team wide movement speed for rotations and chases
Burst protection with Sound Barrier or Summer Anthem
Disengage with Soundwave and Push Off
weak: Very poor wave clear

Aggressive play can get him killed before the fight

good_into.why: Crossfade Healing Boost heals everyone nearby continuously and Amp It Up multiplies it, which is the best answer to spread chip damage and AoE damage that single target healers cannot cover.
Sound Barrier gives a 1296 point shield to the team and Soundwave, Push Off and speed boost let him peel divers. Summer Anthem can save the team from a wombo.
Soundwave on an 8 second cooldown knocks melee Heroes out of position, Off the Wall resets it, and Heavy Casters turns Push Off into a stun.
Speed Boost makes low mobility Heroes much easier to stick to targets and rotate, and he can pull with Wall Ride to drag away or kite.

bad_into.why: Ground persistent crowd control and root zones catch him as he skates in to save allies. High Five is cancelled by a stun or root and his health pool is small.
Long range single target damage from Raynor or Sgt. Hammer type Heroes punishes him because he must stay in the middle of the team and cannot outheal focused fire with an aura.
Low health pool and no escape except skating on terrain, so assassins who find him without a nearby wall kill him before the fight starts.

Maiev.strengths_note: Spirit of Vengeance and Warden's Cage let her pick targets and escape.
wants: A tank who chains CC on pulled targets
Assassins with avoidable AoE who benefit from the pull
AoE healers who follow her engage
Teammates who do not need her for solo lane
gives: A reliable non tank initiator
Pick potential with Containment Disc
Fast mercenary camp clearing
Peel with Warden's Cage and Vault of the Wardens
weak: Predictable engage that CC or blinds shut down
No self sustain
Limited solo lane and low single target damage
Low damage output when Fan of Knives misses

good_into.why: Spirit of Vengeance through a bush into Umbral Bind tethers and pulls heroes out of position, and Containment Disc silences one of them for 5.5 seconds.
Melee heroes bunch up for easy double Fan of Knives hits, and Bladed Armor stacks armor against their autos.
Umbral Bind holds targets inside the circle for 2.5 seconds and Warden's Cage or Containment Disc locks down heroes with no escape.
Naisha's Memento is the fastest early camp clear, and Containment Disc can hold a lone hero while her team collapses.

bad_into.why: A stun, silence or blind stops the Spirit of Vengeance and Umbral Bind combo, and blink cannot be used while rooted, silenced or stunned.
Mobile ranged heroes refuse the tether or move out of Fan of Knives range so she cannot reset her cooldown.
Her single target damage is low, so a sustain healer heals through the Fan of Knives chip.
She has no self heal, so burst assassins can punish a mistake after the combo and Vault of the Wardens is brief.

Mal'Ganis.strengths_note: Vampiric Touch gives strong sustain and Night Rush catches squishies.
Mal'Ganis.weaknesses_note: Many abilities and both heroics are easy to interrupt and roots stop him.
wants: mage or burst that follows his sleep and stun (Kel'Thuzad, Illidan, Sonya)
a second source of crowd control to cover interrupts
flank routes on the map
gives: multi hero sleep and stun setup
enemy backline disruption
healer independent frontline
weak: heroics easily interrupted
low range engage
needs a flank, weak on open maps
weak to kiting and roots

good_into.why: Night Rush gives 50 percent speed, passes through heroes and sleeps them for 2.5 seconds. Seeker Swarm sleeps everyone nearby for 2.5 seconds, so the backline is easy to lock.
Fel Claws third slash stuns and Night Rush closes the gap, so low mobility heroes cannot get away. Blind as a Bat spams stuns on the same target.
Dark Conversion swaps health percentages, so it deals huge damage to big health pools like Stitches. Will of Tichondrius also steals 4 percent of enemy health.
Necrotic Embrace gives armor and Vampiric Touch heals when he is hit while Fel Claws stuns and Night Rush beats melee heroes to a target.

bad_into.why: The guide names Lunara and Hanzo. Every engage tool has short range so a kiter keeps him out and he cannot use Vampiric Touch.
Night Rush, Carrion Swarm and Dark Conversion are all interrupted by stuns, roots and silences (Deckard Cain root, Garrosh Warlord's Challenge). If Carrion Swarm is interrupted he usually dies.
Illidan, Zeratul and similar heroes are hard to hit with Fel Claws and he cannot peel them off his team.
He must reach the enemy to heal, and ranged poke wears him down before he can use Vampiric Touch. Carrion Swarm is his only reset and needs a 100 second cooldown.

Malfurion.strengths_note: Regrowth, Entangling Roots and Tranquility give lots of healing and CC.
wants: Allies who protect him from dive
Mana hungry or cooldown reliant Heroes for Innervate, such as casters
Wave clear from others
Crowd control to chain with Entangling Roots
gives: Sustain healing that scales through long fights
Area root, sleep and silence
Innervate mana and cooldown speed up
Cleanse from Nature's Cure
weak: Struggles against burst damage
Vulnerable to dive
Low wave clear

Moonfire healing needs enemies in range

good_into.why: Regrowth is a 20 second heal over time on several allies and Tranquility plus Serenity covers AoE damage. Long chip damage that a burst healer cannot cover is his best matchup.
Entangling Roots follows up any crowd control on clumped melee Heroes, Emerald Dreams extends it with sleep, and Twilight Dream silence shuts down melee abilities for 3 seconds.
Nature's Cure removes stuns, roots and slows from every ally with Regrowth, at unlimited range. It does not give Unstoppable.
Roots and Hindering Moonfire slow punish dashers who commit, and Regrowth heals divers wherever they go because Moonfire heal ignores distance.

bad_into.why: Regrowth spreads healing over 20 seconds, so a focused dive kills before it ticks. He has no escape and his own Regrowth needs Rejuvenation to be useful on himself.
Low mobility and a squishy body with no Unstoppable. Assassins who cut through the frontline remove the healer first.
Hard to hit Moonfire and Roots on Heroes that stay at range, so Regrowth healing from Moonfire dries up and his low damage cannot punish them.

Malthael.strengths_note: Wraith Strike, Soul Rip and Death Shroud give pick and team fight value.
Malthael.weaknesses_note: Lacks reliable dive and is vulnerable to CC.
Malthael.owner_notes: A bruiser who is great at camps, double soaking and fighting high health heroes. In team fights he can sustain enough to kill a team if they lack CC to pin him and have no healing reduction. Very weak to CC plus burst damage and to reduced healing, and has no CC or escape.
wants: Displacement or crowd control to hold targets so Last Rites and marks stick
A tank to absorb the first burst so he can enter later
Reliable cooldown or mana help (Malfurion Innervate, Ana Nano Boost)
Not a team that needs his waveclear and zoning replaced by a tank
gives: Wave clear and mercenary camp capture while double soaking
Percent health pressure that counters high health frontlines
Revealing marks on enemies including stealth heroes
Finish potential from range with Last Rites
weak: Easily kited
Low max health and little burst early
No utility beyond damage
Marks are removed by Blaze's Bunker Drop and by his own Inevitable End

good_into.why: Reaper's Mark deals 2 percent max health per second and Soul Rip heals for 4 percent of a heroic target's max health, so big health pools feed both his damage and his sustain. Mortality adds 8 percent max health on Wraith Strike.
Melee heroes cannot kite him, stay inside his cleave and Soul Rip range, and are easy to mark with several targets at once, which is when Soul Rip heals the most.

Touch of Death cuts healing on marked heroes by 50 percent, which the guide names for Diablo, Dehaka and Sonya style sustain and for double healer comps. Without the talent the percent damage still survives some healing.
Last Rites executes anyone under 33 percent health from range after a 2 second delay and refunds cooldown on kills, so a poked backline target is a finish for him.

bad_into.why: Wraith Strike only works on marked targets and Death Shroud is a slow skillshot, so nimble ranged heroes keep him unmarked and out of Soul Rip range.
Several ranged heroes make Soul Rip hit few targets (one target heals little) and let them poke his low max health before he connects. Ethereal Existence does not help against ability damage.
He has no reliable escape except Inevitable End on a 20 second cooldown. Stuns and silences hold him while burst kills a low health pool.
Low maximum health and a mark that does nothing for his defence early. Shroud of Wisdom needs 1.5 seconds of warning, so surprise burst lands first.
Poke wears him down before he engages and his Soul Rip healing only comes when he is touching enemies. The guide says he does poorly into ranged heroes.

Medivh.strengths_note: Portal, Raven Form and Poly Bomb add pick potential and global presence.
wants: dive heroes that use Force of Will (Illidan, Sonya, Tracer, tanks)
area crowd control or burst to follow Ley Line Seal (Diablo, Kael'thas)
a healer that can sustain the rest of the team
a team that communicates Portal
gives: damage immunity on one ally
Portal for engage and escape
map scouting with Raven Form
area crowd control with two heroic options
weak: low sustain, no team heal
Ley Line Seal is a dodgeable high risk heroic
skill intensive
weak wave clear and solo lane
measured win rate 0.443

good_into.why: Poly Bomb silences and stops attacks for 2 seconds and spreads to nearby heroes. The guide says it punishes Tracer and Genji, and Force of Will protects his own dive hero.

Melee heroes clump on a target, so Poly Bomb spreads several times and Arcane Explosion (up to 315 extra) with Circle of Protection hits the pile. Ley Line Seal in a corridor holds them for a team follow up.
Portal puts his dive heroes on the backline from an unexpected angle with Raven Form scouting, and Force of Will makes them Invulnerable for 1.5 seconds on arrival.
Ley Line Seal puts the capture platform in Time Stop for 3 seconds so a camp can be stolen, and Portal moves the team to an objective faster than the enemy.

bad_into.why: The guide says he is susceptible to damage over time: poison keeps ticking after Force of Will ends. One ally at a time and a 9 second cooldown do not hold a whole team against chip damage.
A root or stun at the Portal entrance stops allies or himself, and Ley Line Seal has a slow travel animation that is easy to dodge.
Poly Bomb and Force of Will only have value when his team can reach the enemy. A kiter that is not clumped does not spread Poly Bomb.

Mei.strengths_note: Ice Wall, Icing and Blizzard give strong zoning, lane control and poke for a tank.
Mei.weaknesses_note: Fragile for a tank and dependent on her Ice Wall combos.

a second engage so her engage is not alone (Maiev)
terrain or force walls that keep enemies inside Blizzard
gives: wide area stun and slow control
Ice Wall to split the enemy team
armor and speed for the team with Skating Away
disengage with Icing and Snow Blind
weak: weak to high mobility heroes
weak to roots and knockbacks
weak to shield breaking and percent damage
slow delayed abilities

good_into.why: Slows from Snow Blind, Icing and Black Ice set up the Blizzard stun and Avalanche, so heroes without a dash cannot leave. The guide says she punishes heroes who lack mobility.
Snow Blind blinds, Icing knocks back and slows by 80 percent, Cooling Servos slows autos and Skating Away gives 50 armor. Basic attack melee heroes lose their damage and cannot chase.
Cryo-Freeze (1104 shield, Unstoppable, heals 35 percent) and Ice Wall as a time stop frees her team from a dive. Flash Freeze gives a second use.
Avalanche with Cascade averages about 500 damage, and Ice Wall with Shatter does 210 plus 25 armor reduction. She is a good engage that splits their tank from the team.

bad_into.why: The guide says her peeling tools do nothing against Tracer type heroes. Blizzard is delayed and a dash escapes the stun.
Poke from a long distance (Li-Ming) wears her down before she can engage, and Cryo-Freeze is a stationary 3 second cooldown of 40 seconds.
Root and knockback (Malfurion, E.T.C.) stop Icing during the slide. Cryo-Freeze can cover only one.
Her damage is spread chip. A strong sustain healer can ignore Blizzard ticks, Polar Vortex and Snow Blind.

Mephisto.strengths_note: Lightning Nova and Durance of Hate give strong team fight area damage.
Mephisto.weaknesses_note: Low mobility and relies on cooldowns.
